title: API config fallback + routing scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Working scratchpad for a compact config shape that describes routing + fallback policies at the API route level.
- Goal: single source of truth for how requests are routed across model variants, regions, and capacity tiers with automatic fallback behaviors. Mostly focused on Hosted + Dedicated compatibility.

Constraints / goals:
- Config must be human-editable (YAML-ish) and small enough to surface in Console.
- Runtime needs to quickly evaluate policy (O(1) checks per request) - no heavy policy engines.
- Support per-route overrides plus global defaults.
- Support: model variant fallback, region fallback, capacity-tier fallback, and custom pre-conditions (latency budget, token budget, auth tier).
- Telemetry hooks: route_id + chosen_path + reason for fallback (for SLO / billing).

Quick ASCII diagram (request flow):

  Client -> Gateway (auth, quotas) -> Router evaluate(route.policy)
                                 |-> route.primary (fast, quantized)
                                 |-> route.fallbacks[0] (higher cost)
                                 |-> route.fallbacks[1] (remote region)

When primary fails or is unavailable: fallback sequence tried in-order. If none succeed, field "response_fallback": "synthetic-503" or "enqueue"

Config shape (sketch, human YAML-like):

route: generate-summary
  id: "generate-summary"
  match: "/v1/generate-summary"
  defaults: # global defaults can be overridden per-route
    latency_budget_ms: 250
    token_budget: 2048
    allow_cross_region: true
  policy:
    primary:
      model: "redwood/rtx-1b-qat"
      region: "us-west-2"
      capacity_tier: "dedicated"
      preconditions:
        - type: "health" # runtime health check boolean
        - type: "kv_cache_miss_only" # only route to primary if cache miss
    fallbacks:
      - model: "redwood/rtx-1b-int8"
        region: "us-west-2"
        capacity_tier: "shared"
        reason_codes: ["fallback_quantize", "burst"]
      - model: "redwood/rtx-3b"
        region: "us-east-1"
        capacity_tier: "shared"
        preconditions: ["allow_cross_region"]
    response_on_failure: "synthetic-503" # options: synthetic-503 | enqueue | cached-response | escalate

Notes on semantics:
- preconditions: small whitelist of runtime-evaluable predicates (health, token_count_lt, kv_cache_miss_only, auth_level_ge). Avoid Turing-complete expressions.
- reason_codes: optional tags emitted to telemetry to explain which fallback path triggered.
- capacity_tier: informs payment and SLA logic in billing/console.
- allow_cross_region: default false at org level; can be enabled per-route or per-policy.

Example: evaluation rules (pseudocode):
- Evaluate primary.preconditions: if all true, attempt primary. If RPC succeeds within latency_budget, return. If it times out or returns 5xx, record reason and try next fallback.
- If primary never attempted (precondition false), still emit telemetry "skipped-primary:reason".

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Ordering model vs region vs capacity-cost: should policy author specify explicit order (current sketch) or weights + scoring?
  - Explicit order is cheap to evaluate and simpler for users.
  - Weighted scoring allows optimal cost vs latency but requires scoring function and more runtime CPU.
- How to express "partial fallback" (only fall back for certain prompt types or token length)? Need a small expression language or typed conditions.
- Failure modes: if a fallback path exists but is rate-limited, should we skip it or enqueue? Need backpressure semantics.
- Security: allow_cross_region must be gated by org policy + admin approval (console flag).

Telemetry / logging fields to emit per request:
- request_id, route_id, primary_model, chosen_model, chosen_region, fallback_chain_attempted (list), final_status (ok | partial | failed), latency_ms, reason_codes (list)

Short-term implementation plan:
- (P0) Finalize minimal config shape (this doc) and validate with Console UX (Jamie).
- (P0) Add lightweight precondition evaluator in runtime (health, kv_cache_miss, token_count).
- (P1) Implement ordered fallback execution with telemetry and reason_codes.
- (P2) Add console UI for per-route fallback ordering and a preview/simulate button.

Todos / next steps:
- Circle back with Jamie to iterate UI copy + ensure shape fits Console constraints (3/18).
- File a tiny RFC in Confluence with sample routes and edge cases (me).
- Create a Linear task for runtime changes: INF-xxx (runtime router + telemetry).

Scratch notes (quick heuristics):
- Keep policy size < 1KB per route. Many customers will have tens-hundreds of routes.
- Expose a developer-friendly SDK helper that compiles a high-level policy (e.g., prefer-cheapest-with-latency-slo) into this explicit ordered format.
- Consider a global "fallback_policy_profile" that maps to reusable lists of fallbacks.

Unresolved ideas to revisit:
- Allow last-resort synthetic responses (templated) to avoid 503s for user-facing features. Need guardrails to avoid hallucinated content.
- Support gradual rollout: if primary is flagged for canary, route X% of traffic to primary and (1-X) to fallback. That suggests adding a sampling precondition: "traffic_sample_pct: 10".

End of scratchpad.

-- Lee

References mentioned during notes: Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234, ticket JIRA-INF-987, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/458
